source.model: CAMService global atmospheric composition forecast (area-level model data)

derivedIndiaAqi.label: model-derived indicative India AQI estimate
derivedIndiaAqi.note: CPCB-style breakpoints applied to CAMS model data with documented averaging-window coverage. This is NOT an official CPCB AQI and not a station reading.

caveats: Modelled area-level forecast (CAMS via Open-Meteo), not a CPCB station reading; street-level values can differ substantially.
Global forecast grid is coarse; conditions can vary by street, time and indoor environment.
US AQI (Open-Meteo) and the model-derived indicative India AQI estimate are different systems and are never merged.

breathe.title: Move outdoor time to the cleaner window
breathe.instruction: Schedule today's outdoor errands, walks or play time inside the forecast cleaner window instead of the peak-pollution hours.
assumptions: Model forecast timing is approximate and can shift during the day.
Applies only to activities that can be rescheduled.
breathe.methodology: Selected only when the hourly PM2.5 forecast shows a sufficiently cleaner contiguous window; see lib/planner/window.ts and docs/DATA_METHODOLOGY.md.

source.name: WHO - Air pollution, personal interventions and risk communication

breathe.why: Hourly PM2.5 forecast for Delhi shows a potentially better window around 2026-11-28T14:00 to 2026-11-28T15:00: forecast mean ~89.4 ug/m3 vs ~224.7 ug/m3 in the next hours (-60%).

impact.display: Roughly 45 minutes of optional outdoor time can move to a cleaner period (shifting outdoor time into the cleaner window). No precise health benefit is claimed.
impact.qualitative: Exposure-reduction action; benefit is qualitative and depends on actual activity timing.

breathe.title: Keep sensitive members' activity indoors today
breathe.instruction: Shift children's outdoor play and older family members' outdoor exertion to indoor alternatives during the polluted hours.
assumptions: General public-health information; not personalised medical advice.
breathe.methodology: Boosted when the household flags a more sensitive member and the category is Poor or worse. Never states a diagnosis or a health percentage.

source.name: WHO - Air pollution, personal interventions and risk communication

breathe.why: The household includes a more sensitive member and the indicative category is very poor; shifting their outdoor activity today is the precaution the WHO advisory logic supports.

impact.display: Roughly 90 minutes of optional outdoor time can move to a cleaner period (moving a sensitive member's outdoor time indoors for the day). No precise health benefit is claimed.
impact.qualitative: Exposure-reduction action; benefit is qualitative and depends on actual activity timing.

breathe.title: Keep windows shut during peak hours
breathe.instruction: Keep windows and doors closed during the highest-pollution hours today, then air the home out only when the forecast improves.
assumptions: Indoor sources still need ventilation later; this is a peak-hours measure only.
If your home has strong indoor smoke sources, closing windows alone will not fix air quality.
breathe.methodology: Triggered when outdoor category is Very Poor or Severe AND no sufficiently cleaner ventilation window exists in the forecast.

source.name: US EPA - Air cleaners and air filters for the home

breathe.why: With very poor levels in Delhi and only a short cleaner window in the forecast, keeping windows closed during the worst hours limits outdoor PM entering your home.

impact.display: Keeps the worst outdoor hours from raising indoor PM; qualitative benefit only.
impact.qualitative: Indoor source control reduces the source itself; no percentage reduction is claimed without a measurement in your home.

indoor.title: Stop indoor smoke sources
indoor.instruction: Do not smoke, burn incense/dhoop, or use mosquito coils indoors today; find smoke-free alternatives for the rest of the season.
indoor.costNote: No cost; substitutes (mosquito repellent lotions, electric vaporisers) cost about the same or less than coils over a season (estimate).
assumptions: Applies only to sources the household actually uses.
No percentage reduction is claimed; benefit depends on how much the source is used.
indoor.methodology: Source control is the highest-priority indoor measure in EPA guidance: removing the source beats diluting it. Boosted when the profile flags smoking, incense or coils.

source.name: US EPA - Indoor air quality basics

indoor.why: Your profile flags indoor smoke sources (smoking/incense/mosquito coils). Removing the source is the single most effective indoor step per EPA guidance, and today's very poor outdoor air makes indoor smoke worse, not better.

impact.display: Removes the indoor PM source itself; benefit scales with how much the source was used. No percentage claimed.
impact.qualitative: Indoor source control reduces the source itself; no percentage reduction is claimed without a measurement in your home.

indoor.title: Run the kitchen exhaust while cooking
indoor.instruction: Turn on the exhaust fan or chimney that vents outdoors before you start cooking, and leave it running a few minutes after; keep the kitchen door closed so fumes do not spread.
indoor.costNote: No cost if an exhaust fan is already installed.
assumptions: Only applies when the fan/chimney actually vents outdoors, not recirculating.
Electricity cost is small but not zero.
indoor.methodology: Cooking (especially frying) is a major indoor PM source; EPA guidance prioritises venting pollutants outdoors. Boosted when the profile flags frequent frying.

source.name: US EPA - Indoor air quality basics

indoor.why: Frequent frying is flagged in your profile; venting cooking fumes outdoors while they are produced stops them spreading through the home.

impact.display: Keeps cooking PM out of the rest of the home; qualitative benefit only.
impact.qualitative: Indoor source control reduces the source itself; no percentage reduction is claimed without a measurement in your home.

indoor.title: Start with zero-cost source control
indoor.instruction: Before spending on gadgets: remove smoke sources, damp-dust, cook with the exhaust on, and keep the most-used room closed and clean.
assumptions: Source control is the first-line measure regardless of budget.
indoor.methodology: Prioritised for households with zero or low budget and no purifier (EPA source-control hierarchy). No devices are promoted as certified protection.

source.name: US EPA - Indoor air quality basics

indoor.why: Source control comes before any device purchase in EPA guidance.

impact.display: Targets indoor sources directly; no percentage claimed.
impact.qualitative: Indoor source control reduces the source itself; no percentage reduction is claimed without a measurement in your home.

emission.title: Share the car ride
emission.instruction: Carpool with colleagues or neighbours heading the same way, so the same trip carries more people in one vehicle.
emission.costNote: No cost; usually saves money per person.
assumptions: Impact assumes ~3 occupants sharing the car; adjust mentally if different.
emission.methodology: Vehicle emission factor divided by occupancy in lib/impact/emissions.ts, with the assumption documented on the card.
emission.why: Your two-wheeler commute can carry more people in the same vehicle; sharing splits the per-person emissions of the same trip.

impact.display: Estimated ~0.74 kg CO2e/day avoided for your 8 km one-way trips (two-wheeler -> shared car / carpool). Applies to your trip, not to the city's air quality.

numeric.formula: distance_km x (baseline 0.1031 - alternative 0.0567 kg CO2e per person-km) x 2 trips (carpool: vehicle factor / 3 occupants)
assumptions: Indicative public emission factors, not India-certified measured values.
Direct tailpipe CO2e only; no upstream fuel/electricity production included.
Assumes 2 one-way trips per day for this mode shift.

source.name: UK DEFRA/BEIS GHG conversion factors 2024 - average car (unknown fuel)

emission.title: Take a remote work/meeting day
emission.instruction: Move one commute day per week to remote work or virtual meetings if your school or employer allows it.
assumptions: Requires schedule flexibility; not offered to fixed-schedule households.
Impact needs a trip distance to be computed numerically.
emission.methodology: Numeric impact uses the same documented mode-shift formula; without distance the card shows qualitative copy only.
emission.why: One remote day removes the commute trips entirely that day - the largest single-day cut available to a commuting household.

impact.display: Fewer vehicle-km for your trips (two-wheeler -> no regular commute). No numeric estimate shown because trip distance is not provided or the shift is not lower-emitting.
impact.qualitative: A numeric CO2e estimate requires a trip distance and documented factors; both are withheld rather than guessed.

emission.title: Switch off while waiting
emission.instruction: Turn the engine off when parked outside school, shops or gates; idling for more than ~10 seconds wastes more fuel than restarting.
assumptions: No numeric CO2 claim; the benefit depends on idling time avoided.
emission.methodology: Anti-idling is a standard practical measure (also part of the community bulletin). No fabricated percentage is attached.

source.name: UK DEFRA/BEIS GHG conversion factors 2024 (cold-start/idling methodology notes)

emission.why: Idling outside schools and shops burns fuel and emits at kerb height where children breathe; switching off is free.

impact.display: Eliminates idling emissions during waits; no numeric claim without knowing your idling minutes.
